quote: looked at my energy bill, and my energy bills are really, really low.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior look at her home/bill by someone, but rep doesn't press on who, what was shown, or what the outcome was.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be deliberately not chasing this because the customer is already mid-objection and he's trying to get to the bill number first — but he never returns to it even after the bill is captured.
coaching_implication: When a customer references a prior look, immediately ask 'who did that for you?' before anything else — this is qualification data being handed over for free.

quote: Pardon me? Did you look from somebody with Ion?
stewart_read: Second touch on the same prior-contact thread; customer says she can't remember and rep drops it entirely rather than asking what company or when.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be the rep judged this a dead end given her uncertain answer — reasonable in isolation, but no second attempt was made anywhere else in the call.
coaching_implication: Follow 'maybe, I can't remember' with a concrete anchor question — 'was it recent, do you recall the company name' — rather than moving straight to bill amount.

quote: it doesn't get any higher than $60
stewart_read: A genuinely low bill is captured but the rep does nothing with it — no flip, no curiosity hook about how a low bill customer could still benefit or offset future increases.
coaching_implication: Even a low bill has a flip: 'even at $60 in winter, imagine locking that in at zero for the next 25 years' — instead the rep let it stand as proof the deal doesn't work.

quote: so you you don't think it'll make sense?
stewart_read: Textbook trigger for a flip ('it's too expensive' analog: 'it won't make sense') but rep restates it as a question instead of inverting it.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be trying to get her to self-confirm before pivoting to the no-upfront-cost line at 01:21 — but that line came too late and wasn't tied back to this moment.
coaching_implication: On 'won't make sense' objections, invert immediately: 'what doesn't make sense is paying the utility more every year for power you could lock in at a flat rate.'

quote: So so go ahead and take me off your call list, but I appreciate that I I very much appreciate solar energy
stewart_read: Customer explicitly states she worked in green building and loves solar — a values-aligned lead that self-disqualified purely on the bill math, not on interest.
coaching_implication: This is exactly the profile where curiosity about actual numbers (not features) could have re-opened her — rep should have asked to just show her the real design given her stated affinity, instead of accepting the opt-out immediately.

quote: Okay. I can take you off the list. You have a great day.
stewart_read: Call ends with a concession and no attempt at an alternative (email follow-up, revisit next season, roofing/other services) before honoring the removal request.
alternative_hypothesis: Removal requests should generally be honored, so conceding itself isn't wrong — but the rep made zero attempt beforehand to re-engage her stated solar enthusiasm.
coaching_implication: Before honoring an opt-out, make one more values-based attempt given her own words ('I very much appreciate solar energy') rather than closing immediately.
